newsitem.title: CHINA: SHANGHAI B SHARES UP AT NOON ON YITAI COAL DEBUT.
newsitem.headline: SHANGHAI B SHARES UP AT NOON ON YITAI COAL DEBUT.

text.p: Shanghai's foreign currency B shares rose slightly in morning trading on Friday, boosted by buying of newly listed Inner Mongolia Yitai Coal Co Ltd, brokers said.
Although Yitai Coal hit some profit-taking after opening strongly, the stock still closed the morning up $0.035 or 8.60 percent to $0.442 compared with an offer price of $0.4073, they said.
The B index ended the morning up 0.392 points or 0.53 percent to 74.574 points with healthy turnover of $11.614 million compared with $4.515 million on Thursday.
"Trading focused on the two newly listed B shares," said a broker with a foreign securities firm in Shanghai.
Besides Yitai Coal, investors also bought shares of Shanghai Zhenhua Port Machinery Co Ltd, which listed earlier this week.
Zhenhua Port rose $0.030 or 5.17 percent to $0.610 on volume of around 4.4 million shares, making it the second most actively traded B share in morning trading.
Yitai Coal was the morning's most actively traded share on strong volume of around 15.9 million shares.

"Investors were positive on Yitai," said an analyst at a foreign securities firm in Shanghai. "There's strong demand for coal in China and the government is also trying to develop Inner Mongolia, which will benefit the company."
Of 47 B shares, 40 shares traded in the morning with 25 up, eight down and seven unchanged.
Shanghai Diesel Engine Co Ltd was the star, rising $0.022 or 8.87 percent to $0.270.
Brokers said Diesel Engine's position at the top of the gainers list -- ahead of the two newcomers -- showed interest in older shares might be returning.
Domestic currency A shares rose amid an improvement in market sentiment on increased trading volume, brokers said.
The A index gained 11.738 points or 0.94 percent to 1,266.929 points on turnover of 2.327 billion yuan, against 1.283 billion on Thursday morning.
The SSE30 blue chip gained 57.808 points or 1.54 percent to 3,806.812 points.

Brokers said both A and B share market sentiment has improved, helped by the strong performance of Chinese firms listed in Hong Kong and optimistic reports about economic reforms ahead of a Communist Party congress in September or October.
